source.title: SelfPAB: large-scale pre-training on accelerometer data for human activity recognition
source.authors: Aleksej Logacjov; Sverre Herland; Astrid Ustad; Kerstin Bach

record.tranche_reason: The study extends data-scaling experiments to accelerometer-based human activity recognition and reports downstream performance across pre-training data quantities. It does not test language-model loss scaling or fit a power law.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are downstream HAR F1-scores across SelfPAB pre-training data quantities. The study does not measure held-out language-model loss, parameter-count or compute scaling, power-law fits, or extrapolation from small runs. Its statement that pre-training hours seem to scale with downstream performance is an analogy to language-model results, not a test of language-model loss scaling.
record.test_reason: The study varies unique pre-training data (10 h to 100k h, fixed gradient steps) for a ~60M transformer on accelerometer spectrograms. It reports downstream HAR F1 at each size, which bears on V6 in a new, non-text setting. It fits no power law, reports no upstream loss sweep, and varies neither parameters nor compute, so V1–V5 and V7 are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that more unique pre-training data improves downstream HAR, with 100k h best. They add that gains beyond 1k h are marginal (suggesting convergence) and that 10k h is worse than 1k h on HARTH. They also judge the data-collection cost high relative to the gain, and did not test beyond 100k h.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales accelerometer pre-training data and evaluates downstream HAR F1-score; it does not measure language-model held-out loss or fit scaling laws.
record.method_sensitivity: The data-quantity trend differs by downstream dataset: HARTH v1.2 has a reported dip at 10k hours, while HAR70+ is described as improving as hours increase. Exact intermediate F1 values are shown only in plots.

fits_no_version.finding: All five data sizes get the same number of gradient steps, so smaller sets are repeated up to 500k epochs. The comparison is unique-data quantity at fixed compute under heavy repetition. The authors call gains beyond 1k h marginal and suggest convergence, possibly tied to subject count.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At fixed compute, adding unique pre-training data beyond ~1k hours yields diminishing downstream gains in sensor-based self-supervised models.

record.problems: The study reports only five pre-training data quantities and does not fit a power law or make extrapolations. Intermediate values in the data-scaling plots are not stated numerically in the text. The authors also note that they did not investigate more than 100k hours.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant data-scaling results left out. Other downstream datasets are reported for the 100k model but do not vary pre-training data quantity.

untested.parts: Whether downstream gains are predictable (fitted trend or extrapolation); pretraining loss as a predictor; scaling in parameters or compute; language-model downstream tasks.
No held-out pre-training loss reported across data sizes; no parameter or compute sweep.
Other modality, but no power-law fit of loss or performance against data.
No comparison of fits or exponents.

missing.what: Numeric F1 at 100, 1k and 10k hours for both datasets: Fig. 6 only. The text gives only 78.7% for HARTH at 'at least 100 hours' and 73.1% for HAR70+ at 10 h.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not in the text-LM domain. V6 is applied here as a new setting (T3), which is a generous reading; a stricter reading would place it under fits_no_version. The authors cite Kaplan et al. only as an analogy. Fixed gradient steps confound data size with repetition. Upstream validation loss across sizes is not reported.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pre-training loss sweep over parameters, tokens, or compute.
No power-law fit on small runs or prediction of larger runs.
No fixed-compute comparison or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
No controlled depth, width, or architecture comparison at fixed parameter count.
The study evaluates accelerometer pre-training, but does not test whether a power-law loss form holds in another modality or training regime.
Tests downstream HAR F1-score against pre-training data quantity only; does not test downstream language-model tasks, pre-training loss as a predictor, or out-of-range prediction.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents, nor test of setup-dependent power-law bends.

relationships.condition: HAR70+ downstream, SelfPAB pre-trained on 10 h to 100k h of HUNT4
relationships.reason: F1 rises from 73.1% (10 h) to 78.5% (100k h), increasing with hours, with larger gains before 1k h (r7–r10).
relationships.display_finding: F1 increases from 73.1% with 10 hours to 78.5% with 100,000 hours, with larger gains before 1,000 hours.

relationships.condition: HARTH v1.2 downstream, 10 h to 100k h
relationships.reason: The gain is concentrated at 1k h. 10k h is worse than 1k h, and further data improves F1 only marginally, so the trend is non-monotonic and saturating (r3–r5).
relationships.display_finding: Most gains arrived by 1k hours, performance worsened at 10k hours, and further data produced only marginal F1 improvements.
